summary: First wooden fire tower in Kentucky, built by the Division of Forestry in Trigg County; register says it was possibly cleared in the early to mid 1980s.

facts.design: wooden tower of four 50-foot creosoted poles with other creosoted lumber
facts.status_note: Register says the tower rotted and was possibly cleared during early to mid 1980s road work; no removal record found

access.note: Site lies inside Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area, a public recreation area; the register does not describe access to the site itself

events.note: Registered November 2, 2009 on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register; nominated by Trenton C. Girard

notes_for_editor: No build year: the FFLOS page has no Built field and two searches found no year, so there is no built event and the story does not give a date. Removal is the register's 'possibly cleared' wording, not a documented removal, so no removed event is recorded. Access level 'public' is inferred from the site lying inside the NRA; the register says nothing about access to the spot. A Library of Congress photo record (loc.gov/item/2020722377, 2020, titled as a fire tower in the Kentucky portion of Land Between the Lakes, Trigg County) could not be fetched (HTTP 403). It is not used, and an editor may want to check whether it shows this tower. The Trigg Observation Tower in Illinois is a different structure and is not used. No photos added.
